commit.message:
Claude/actenon kernel mcp setup qolk0h (#21)

* build: make plain install + pytest work; require kernel >=1.0.0

- httpx is now a runtime dependency. fastapi.testclient refuses to
  import without it, so `pip install . && pytest` (the README's
  machine-verified promise) failed with 6 collection errors.
- actenon-kernel floor raised 0.1.0 -> 1.0.0 and uv.lock refreshed
  (0.1.0 -> 1.2.1). Kernel 0.1.0, which CI was locked to, registers
  its own `actenon` console script (shadowing permit's unified CLI:
  `actenon protect ...` was "invalid choice") and ships no
  actenon.boundary, which put BoundaryMiddleware on its structural
  fallback path.
- uv.lock was also stale against pyproject (`uv lock --check` failed:
  pytest-asyncio runtime dep missing from the lock).
- verify-claims now runs the plain-install promise literally in a
  clean venv instead of only asserting a dependency name.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* chore: remove stray uv.lock.bak

An old lockfile (permit 0.1.0, kernel from git, protocol from a
../actenon-protocol directory source) that nothing references. It is
not a usable lock for this checkout and only invites confusion.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* docs: make the README hero quickstart run; correct signing claims

- The hero quickstart granted scopes=["issue.create"] but performs
  "github.issue.create", so it raised ExecutionRefusedError("out of
  scope") instead of printing "succeeded  final". The scope now names
  the action it performs (scope matching is left strict). A new test
  executes the README snippet verbatim and asserts its documented
  output.
- Grants are HMAC-SHA256 only, over sorted-key compact JSON; the README
  claimed "HMAC-SHA256 (v0) or Ed25519 (pilot) over ACTENON-JCS-STRICT-1".
  Ed25519 applies to PCCBs, and only once a keypair is configured;
  otherwise the kernel HMAC dev signer is used. Say so.
- docs/README.md compatibility row: kernel >= 1.0.0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* fix(security): attenuation could widen scope and remove rate limits

Grant.attenuate() treated two widenings as narrowings:

- scopes_allow=[] passed the subset check, but an empty allow list is
  permissive (SPEC §4: only deny is enforced). A child of a grant
  scoped to payment.refund was ALLOWed payment.charge (and anything
  else not denied), via the API or POST /grants/{id}/attenuate.
- rate_max=0 passed `0 > parent.max == False`, but max=0 disables rate
  limiting, so a rate-limited parent could mint an unlimited child.
  Negative values are rejected too.

Both are now refused with ValueError (HTTP 400 on the wire endpoint).
SPEC §6/§13.2 tables state the constraint explicitly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* fix(security): revocation did not reach grandchildren or delegated grants

Revoking a grant only flipped its direct children, and only through
POST /grants/{id}/revoke. A grandchild kept executing after its root
was revoked, and the `permit revoke <agent>` kill switch left every
grant attenuated to another agent id (the default child agent id is
"<agent>+child") fully usable.

- SQLiteStore.reserve() now refuses, inside the same transaction every
  ALLOW goes through, any grant with a revoked ancestor. This holds
  however the ancestor was revoked.
- The HTTP cascade is transitive and denies pending approvals for
  every revoked descendant.
- Reserve refusals mentioning revocation map to FailureCode.REVOKED
  instead of ENGINE_ERROR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* fix(security): budget bypass via non-numeric cost arguments

The gateway and @guard only reserved budget when the cost field was an
int/float. Any other type reserved $0 but was still passed to the tool:
three refund(amount="40") calls against a $50 grant were all ALLOWed
with the budget untouched, and @guard paid out $120 of Decimal("40")
refunds against the same $50.

estimate_cost() is now the single cost estimator for both paths. The
cost field (cost_from, else amount, else cost) must be a finite
int/float/Decimal; anything else (str, None, bool, containers, NaN,
inf) is DENY with rule_matched "cost:invalid" before the PDP runs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* fix(security): threshold approval rules failed open on unreadable amounts

`payment.refund > 20` evaluated float(amount) > 20 and returned False
when float() raised. An amount of NaN (float or "NaN" string, which
compares False) or any non-numeric value skipped the human approval
and the PDP returned ALLOW. Params reach the PDP unfiltered on the
intent path (Actenon.local(), POST /intents/{id}/execute).

An amount that is not a finite number now matches the rule, so the
decision is REQUIRE_APPROVAL. SPEC §5 documents it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* fix(security): broker's defensive credential redaction never ran

Broker.execute_via_adapter() destroys the credential (blanks
credential.value) in a finally block, then called
_final_redact(response, credential), which read the now-empty value
and returned the response untouched. The documented belt-and-braces
pass was dead code: an adapter whose redact() missed the token put it
straight into provider_evidence (and the receipt/agent response), and
`raw` was not dropped either.

The value is now captured before the call and used for the scrub
(then deleted); `raw` is always dropped; adapter error text is
scrubbed of the credential before it becomes BrokerExecutionError.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* fix(security): configured Ed25519 key silently downgraded to HMAC

resolve_signer() swallowed every error loading the configured Ed25519
key (ACTENON_ED25519_KEY_FILE, an explicit path, or an existing
~/.actenon-permit/ed25519-key.json), and also ignored a configured path
that did not exist, then fell back to HMAC. With ACTENON_SIGNING_KEY
unset that is the kernel's local signer keyed with its public default
secret, so a typo or a truncated key file turned "Ed25519 in
production" into forgeable HS256 PCCBs with no error.

A configured key that is missing or unloadable now raises
Ed25519KeyError. Minting and edge verification already fail closed on
signer errors, so the gateway DENYs instead of executing. Unconfigured
setups still use HMAC as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* fix(security): GitHub adapter owner/repo could re-target the request

owner and repo are interpolated into the REST path unchecked. A call
authorised (and PCCB-bound) as github.issue.create with
repo="example/issues/7/comments#" was sent as
POST /repos/Actenon/example/issues/7/comments, i.e. an issue comment,
an action the grant may deny; "?" and ".." segments re-target it too.

validate_params() now requires GitHub-shaped names (owner:
alphanumeric/hyphen, max 39; repo: [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,100}, not "." or
"..") and rejects anything else with InvalidParametersError before any
request is built.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* fix(security): intent path skipped budget and edge verification

Gateway.execute_intent() (Actenon.local() and POST
/intents/{id}/execute, the recommended on-ramp) did not do what the
README's hero path promises:

- est_cost was hard-coded to 0.0, so no budget was ever reserved: a
  $1000 refund against a $10 grant succeeded.
- The PCCB was minted and discarded; verify_pccb_at_edge() was never
  called before the broker resolved the credential, and the broker
  executed a freshly derived Action (new action_id, cost 0) rather than
  the one decided on. The intent's "proof" link was a random id.
- The coordinator reported receipt_received/receipt_verified = True for
  every state ("the broker signs its own receipts") although no receipt
  existed anywhere.

Now the path prices the action with estimate_cost() (non-numeric ->
DENY), looks up the adapter before reserving, verifies the PCCB at the
edge (releasing the reservation and DENYing on failure), executes the
exact decided Action, links the real pccb_id, and releases the
reservation when the broker refuses before any provider call.

On success, brokered adapter calls (intent path and call_tool) return
a kernel execution Receipt plus the intent/PCCB it links to;
receipt_received/receipt_verified are True only then. The receipt
checks out offline:
  actenon-kernel verify-receipt --receipt r.json --intent i.json --pccb p.json
BrokeredResult gains optional `receipt` and `proof` fields.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* test: end-to-end hero path; refuse intent replays before the PDP

tests/test_hero_path_e2e.py drives the README hero path in process:
Actenon.local() grant -> PDP ALLOW -> kernel PCCB -> edge verification
-> adapter executes once -> kernel Receipt that `actenon-kernel
verify-receipt` accepts (linked to the returned intent and PCCB), then
checks that a replay, widened parameters, a revoked grant, an expired
grant and an out-of-scope action are refused without reaching the
adapter.

Replaying an executed intent used to run the PDP first (ALLOW ledger
entry, budget reservation) and only fail on the lifecycle transition
afterwards; execute_intent() now refuses any intent that is not in the
CREATED state up front ("intent:not_executable").

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* fix(security): Boundary Kit accepted any token; protect test faked PASS

BoundaryMiddleware (enforce mode) let a request through with any
X-Actenon-Proof of 16+ characters: with kernel <= 1.2.1 the kernel
BoundaryVerifier checked length only, and with no actenon.boundary
module (kernel 0.1.0) the middleware's own ImportError fallback did the
same. A junk header ran a $1e9 refund handler. Trust roots
(manifest.trusted_issuers) and the request's parameters were never
used, and path parameters were always empty inside the middleware.

`actenon protect test` / `protect quickstart` printed ten hard-coded
check marks per boundary and wrote assurance PASS without sending a
single request; the generated actenon_boundary.py raised NameError on
import (it referenced an undefined `app`).

Middleware (fail closed at every step):
- requests carry the PCCB (X-Actenon-Proof) and the exact Action Intent
  (X-Actenon-Intent); the intent's action, target and every mapped
  parameter must equal what the request carries (path params are now
  derived from the route pattern);
- the kernel verifies the PCCB against that intent and the boundary's
  audience with a trust root: the issuers' Ed25519 JWKs under
  trusted_issuers[].public_keys, or pccb_verifier=. Kernels whose
  BoundaryVerifier binds intents (kernel branch 1f8b482) are used
  directly; older kernels go through PCCBVerifier with the same checks;
- missing kernel verifier, trust root, audience or intent => 403;
  single use keyed on proof identity.
- New boundary.proofs: token format, Ed25519PublicKeyVerifier,
  trust_root_from_issuers, mint_boundary_proof, proof_headers.

protect test / quickstart now run boundary.selftest: real requests
through the middleware per route with a throwaway issuer key (valid,
none, altered params/target, replay, wrong audience, expired,
malformed, forged key, alternate routes), report pass/fail/not-run as
observed, list trust-configuration gaps separately, and exit 1 on any
failure. A test swaps in a fail-open middleware and asserts FAIL. The
generated module exposes protect(app). Boundary tests now present
genuinely minted proofs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* fix(security): bind only real params in PCCBs; let adapter tools price cost_from

- _permit_action_to_kernel_intent() injected "amount": repr(est_cost)
  into the proof-bound parameters whenever the action had no amount
  (e.g. cost_from="amount_minor" or a "cost" field), so the PCCB bound
  a value the caller never sent. It now binds exactly action.params.
- Adapter-backed tools could not declare which parameter carries the
  cost, so on the intent path only amount/cost were priced: an adapter
  taking amount_minor=99,999,999 ran against a 100 budget.
  register_adapter_tool() (gateway registry and Actenon.local client)
  accepts cost_from, and the intent path prices with it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

* fix(security): PCCBs lived as long as their grant (24h in Actenon.local)

The intent/PCCB expiry was the grant's expiry, so a proof minted just
before revocation stayed valid at any edge (e.g. a kernel
ProtectedExecutor) for the rest of the grant's life.

PCCBs now expire PCCB_TTL_SECONDS (120 s) after the action's timestamp,
bounded by the grant's expiry. The window is anchored on action.ts so
the intent rebuilt for edge verification matches the minted one; after
a human approval the gateway restarts it so a slow approver does not
produce a born-expired proof. SPEC §10 documents the residual window.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AWNAfEkZsFvwvUGh6dF8bh

---------

* fix(security): bind only real params in PCCBs; let adapter tools price cost_from

- _permit_action_to_kernel_intent() injected "amount": repr(est_cost)
  into the proof-bound parameters whenever the action had no amount
  (e.g. cost_from="amount_minor" or a "cost" field), so the PCCB bound
  a value the caller never sent. It now binds exactly action.params.
- Adapter-backed tools could not declare which parameter carries the
  cost, so on the intent path only amount/cost were priced: an adapter
  taking amount_minor=99,999,999 ran against a 100 budget.
  register_adapter_tool() (gateway registry and Actenon.local client)
  accepts cost_from, and the intent path prices with it.

* fix(security): PCCBs lived as long as their grant (24h in Actenon.local)

The intent/PCCB expiry was the grant's expiry, so a proof minted just
before revocation stayed valid at any edge (e.g. a kernel
ProtectedExecutor) for the rest of the grant's life.

PCCBs now expire PCCB_TTL_SECONDS (120 s) after the action's timestamp,
bounded by the grant's expiry. The window is anchored on action.ts so
the intent rebuilt for edge verification matches the minted one; after
a human approval the gateway restarts it so a slow approver does not
produce a born-expired proof. SPEC §10 documents the residual window.
